agents.subtitle: Agent installation, enrollment tokens and agent status
agents.install.title: Agent installation
agents.install.step1: Create an enrollment token with the form on the right. The token is shown only once.
agents.install.step2: Choose the server's operating system and run the generated command on the server to be managed:
agents.install.os.rhel: RHEL / CentOS / AlmaLinux / Rocky / Oracle Linux
agents.install.offline_windows: Windows: copy the files to one folder and run this in PowerShell opened as administrator:
agents.install.sudo_hint: Installation requires root. sudo is not needed in a root session; if sudo is not installed (common on CentOS, Debian and Alpine), leave the box unchecked. The Debian and Alpine commands use wget instead of curl. Run the Windows command in PowerShell or a command prompt opened as administrator.
agents.install.step3: The agent registers with the server, sends its inventory and appears on the Server Inventory page within a few minutes.
agents.install.offline_body: Download the files from these addresses, copy them to the server and run the install script with the --binary option:
agents.install.supported_body: Inventory and updates: every distribution using apt (Debian, Ubuntu), dnf/yum (RHEL, AlmaLinux, Rocky Linux), zypper (SUSE, openSUSE) or apk (Alpine) with systemd or OpenRC (including CentOS, Oracle Linux and Fedora), and Windows 10, Windows 11 and Windows Server 2016 / 2019 / 2022 / 2025 (x64, Windows Update). Physical server, VMware, Hyper-V, KVM/Proxmox or cloud makes no difference. Vulnerability scanning: Debian, Ubuntu, AlmaLinux, Rocky Linux, Red Hat Enterprise Linux, SUSE Linux Enterprise, openSUSE Leap, Alpine and Windows (CVEs of pending Microsoft updates; third-party Windows programs are not scanned).

settings.security.require_mfa_hint: When on, users without an authenticator can only open their profile page until they set one up.
settings.risk.max_days_hint: 0 allows acceptance without expiry. Recommended: 365 or less.
mfa.title: Two-factor authentication
mfa.intro: At sign-in, a 6-digit code from an authenticator app (Google Authenticator, Microsoft Authenticator, Aegis, FreeOTP, etc.) is required in addition to the password.
mfa.setup.step1: Open an authenticator app on your phone and add a new account.
mfa.setup.step2: Choose "Enter a setup key" and type this key:
mfa.setup.params: Type: time-based (TOTP), 6 digits, 30 seconds. If the app is on this device:
mfa.setup.step3: Turn on two-factor authentication by entering the code shown in the app and your password.
mfa.enabled: Two-factor authentication is on. Your other sessions were signed out.
mfa.codes_once: Your recovery codes are below and are shown only now. Each can be used once to sign in if you cannot access your phone; keep them in a safe place.
mfa.manage_hint: Enter your password and a valid verification code (or a recovery code).
mfa.recovery_regenerated: New recovery codes generated; the old ones no longer work.
mfa.error.code: The verification code is invalid or expired. Make sure your phone's clock is correct.
mfa.error.setup_again: The setup data is invalid. Please start the setup again.
mfa.error.required: Two-factor authentication is required on this system and cannot be turned off.
mfa.required_notice: Two-factor authentication is required on this system. Set up an authenticator app to continue.
mfa.recovery_used: You signed in with a recovery code. {count} recovery codes left; generate new ones if needed.
mfa.reset_confirm: Remove the authenticator of {email}? All of the user's sessions are signed out.
mfa.login.title: Two-Factor Authentication
mfa.login.heading: Verification code
mfa.login.body: Enter the 6-digit code shown in your authenticator app.
mfa.login.recovery_hint: If you do not have your phone, you can type one of your recovery codes (xxxx-xxxx-xxxx).
mfa.login.invalid: The code is invalid or was already used.
mfa.login.expired: The verification expired. Please sign in again.
mfa.login.too_many: Too many wrong codes. Please sign in again.
language.name: English
language.label: Interface language
language.hint: This choice only affects your dashboard. Emails and system logs stay in the server's default language (PATCHMAN_LOCALE).
settings.backup.title: Automatic backup
settings.backup.enabled: Back up the database automatically every day
settings.backup.hint: Backups are written to the backup directory on the server; the newest backups are kept and older ones deleted. Since they only exist on this server, copy them elsewhere regularly too (PATCHMAN_BACKUP_DIR can point to a separate disk). If the server is down at the backup time, the backup runs when it starts.
backup.none: There are no backups in the backup directory yet.
email.backup_failed.subject: [CRITICAL] netio.patchman: database backup failed
email.backup_failed.heading: Database backup failed
email.backup_failed.body: The automatic backup failed. Check the free disk space and the write permission of the backup directory, then try again with "Back up now" in Settings.
channels.title: Notification channels
channels.subtitle: Also send notifications to Slack, Microsoft Teams, Telegram or your own system (webhook).
channels.secret_note: Webhook addresses and bot tokens are secrets and are not shown in full after saving. To change one, delete the channel and add it again.
channel.field.name: Channel name
channel.field.min_level_hint: Notifications below this level are not sent to this channel.
channel.help.slack: In Slack, create an address for the channel with Apps → Incoming Webhooks (https://hooks.slack.com/services/…).
channel.help.teams: In the Teams channel, create an address with Workflows → "Post to a channel when a webhook request is received". Messages are sent as Adaptive Cards.
channel.help.webhook: Each notification is POSTed as JSON (kind, level, text, url, params, created_at). HTTP is accepted; use HTTPS outside your internal network.
channel.help.secret: If set, the HMAC-SHA256 signature of the request body is sent in the X-Netio-Patchman-Signature: sha256=<hex> header.
channel.help.telegram: Create a bot with @BotFather and add it to the group. A group chat ID starts with a minus sign (-100…), or use a channel name (@channel_name).
channel.created: Channel “{name}” added. Send a test message to check the settings.
channel.unavailable: Notification channels are not active on this server.
channel.error.name: The channel name is required and can be at most 60 characters.
channel.error.url: Enter a valid http:// or https:// address.
channel.error.https: Slack and Teams addresses must start with https://.
channel.error.secret: The signing secret can be at most 200 characters.
channel.error.telegram_chat: The chat ID must be a number (-1001234567890) or @channel_name.
notification.channel_test: This is a test message. Notifications reach this channel.
log.channel.failed: Notification could not be sent to the channel
log.channel.queue_full: The channel queue is full; the notification stays in the notification center only
cli.reset_mfa.done: Two-factor authentication of {email} was removed; the user can sign in with the password alone and set it up again.
